title: Roku’s first OLED TVs are up to $400 off, starting at $699
summary: Roku has launched its first OLED TVs with significant discounts, making the 55-inch Pro Series available starting at $699 and the 65-inch model at $799 with promotional codes. The sets offer competitive OLED picture quality and gaming features at more affordable price points than traditional premium OLED options.
content:
Roku’s new OLED TVs are already marked down. | Image: The Verge	

Roku recently launched its first-ever OLED TVs. The $999 starting price was already impressive for the 55-inch Pro Series model that has a 120Hz refresh rate OLED panel (with four HDMI 2.1 ports and support for Dolby Vision and HDR 10 Plus). The price is even lower right now at Amazon when you enter the code ROKUOLED300 at checkout. It knocks a clean $300 off, as the code indicates, making this the most affordable modern 55-inch OLED you can get right now.
If you’re more of a 65-inch TV kind of person, you’re in luck, as there’s a code that knocks $400 off that model to make it just $799 at checkout. Enter the code ROKUOLED400 to bring the $1,299 65-inch Pro Series down to $799. We haven’t had a chance to test either model, but they seem respectable if you want great picture quality without breaking the bank.
Roku Pro Series OLED (2026)

Where to Buy:

 $999.99 $699.99 at Amazon (55-inch, with code ROKUOLED300)
 $1199.99 $799.99 at Amazon (65-inch, with code ROKUOLED400)

Given that these are Roku TVs, the company’s software is built-in, negating the need to stick a streaming device into one of its HDMI ports, unless you prefer hardware from other brands. The Pro Series includes a backlit Roku remote, and it supports auto low latency mode, and has variable refresh rate (AMD FreeSync Premium) for gaming. There’s a pricier Pro Series LX coming in October starting at $1,299 that claims to be twice as bright as the Pro Series, with a reflection-reducing polarizer and 144Hz refresh rate.

title: Lightspeed targets $250M for new India fund, focusing on early-stage AI
summary: Lightspeed is raising $250M for a new India-focused venture fund, aligning its India investment cycle with global funds and shifting to shorter investment periods. The move reflects growing institutional interest in India's early-stage AI startup ecosystem.
content: The venture firm is aligning its India fundraising cycle with its global funds for the first time, as it shifts to a shorter investment period.

zh.title: Lightspeed瞄准2.5亿美元印度基金，专注早期AI
zh.summary: Lightspeed正在为新的以印度为重点的风险基金筹集2.5亿美元，使其印度投资周期与全球基金保持一致，并转向更短的投资期。这一举措反映了机构投资者对印度早期AI创业生态系统日益增长的兴趣。

title: Here’s the Tesla Semi… again
summary: Tesla's long-awaited Semi truck is finally in volume production as of April 2026, nearly a decade after its 2017 debut. The company held a customer event at its new Semi factory near Gigafactory Nevada, which can produce 50,000 trucks annually, with major customers including PepsiCo, DHL, and others confirmed.
content:
Remember the Tesla Semi? The long-gestating, heavy-duty truck first introduced in concept form in 2017 is finally in volume production as of April 2026 - nearly a decade after its initial introduction. On Thursday evening, the company held yet another event for the Semi to demonstrate to customers and investors that the long wait was finally over. 
The event was held at Tesla's new Semi factory next to Gigafactory Nevada, where the company says it can build 50,000 trucks a year, or 1,000 per week. The purpose was to announce a raft of new (and old) customers for the Semi, including PepsiCo, US Foods, DHL, WattEV, ABF, Einride, IMC, and OK P …

zh.title: 特斯拉Semi又来了
zh.summary: 特斯拉期待已久的Semi卡车自2026年4月起终于进入批量生产，距其2017年首次亮相已近十年。该公司在Gigafactory Nevada附近的新Semi工厂举办了客户活动，该工厂每年可生产5万辆卡车，主要客户包括百事可乐、DHL等已确认。

title: Microsoft is killing off the ‘Copilot Plus PC’ brand
summary: Microsoft and Qualcomm are abandoning the 'Copilot Plus PC' branding just 2.5 years after launch, with new Surface devices no longer carrying the label despite meeting technical requirements. The shift signals the AI differentiation strategy failed to resonate in the market.
content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella introducing the company’s Copilot Plus PC initiative. | Image: Allison Johnson	

Remember when Microsoft wanted everyone to know that "Copilot Plus PCs" were the ones to get, because those were the PCs that that'd have enough built-in AI muscle to get things done? Two and a half years later, Microsoft and Qualcomm seem to be admitting the brand is already dead. 
Windows Central's Zac Bowden reports that even though the new 12-inch Microsoft Surface Pro and 13-inch Surface Laptop technically meet the system requirements for a Copilot Plus PC, Microsoft is not calling them by that name anymore. "These are not called Copilot Plus PCs," Microsoft Surface CVP Brett Ostrom told the publication.

zh.title: 微软放弃'Copilot Plus PC'品牌
zh.summary: 微软和高通在推出2.5年后放弃了'Copilot Plus PC'品牌，新款Surface设备尽管符合技术要求但不再使用该标签。这一转变表明人工智能差异化战略未能在市场上获得认可。
